summary: The Fit to Serve Act amends title 10 of the U.S. Code to bar the armed forces from discriminating against members on the basis of gender identity by denying accession, reenlistment, health care, or continued service or by requiring service in the sex assigned at birth.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends military personnel policy to prohibit gender identity discrimination but contains no provisions related to budgets, appropriations, or spending levels.
No provisions address taxes, tax rates, or revenue policy.

Section 2 prohibits denying 'medically necessary health care coverage' on the basis of gender identity in the Armed Forces. This tangentially touches military healthcare access but does not engage the public/universal vs. private/market-based dimension of the topic.
No relation to firearms regulation or gun rights.
No provisions on immigration, borders, or pathways to citizenship.
No provisions related to abortion access or restrictions.
The bill addresses military personnel policy (accession, retention, and healthcare) but does not alter defense spending levels or budgets.
No environmental or regulatory provisions.
No provisions on welfare programs or entitlements outside the military context.
No education policy provisions.
No drug enforcement or decriminalization measures.
No criminal sentencing or policing reforms.
No trade, tariff, or globalization provisions.
No deficit or debt-reduction measures.

The bill's sole purpose is to insert a new section 975 into title 10 that explicitly prohibits discrimination on the basis of gender identity in all aspects of military service (accession, retention, healthcare, assignments, etc.). This directly expands legal protections for transgender service members.
No foreign aid provisions.
No voting or election-related content.
No technology or privacy regulation provisions.
No labor, union, or employment flexibility provisions.
By mandating non-discrimination on gender identity without any religious exemption language, the bill prioritizes civil-rights protections over potential religious objections in the military setting.
